question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can factor out $5$ from each of the terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{t}^{2}-15t-20 & =5({t}^{2}-3t-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the polynomial ${t}^{2}-3t-4$ in parentheses.

First, we find the factor pairs of the constant term $(-4).$ The constant term is negative, so that means one of the factors is negative and the other is positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & \times (-4) \\ (-1) & \times 4 \\ 2 & \times (-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+(-4) & =-3 & ✓ \\ (-1)+4 & =3 & \times  \\ 2+(-2) & =0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

Using the factor pair identified above, we write the linear term as $-3t=t-4t$ and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-3t-4 & = \\ {t}^{2}+t-4t-4 & = \\ ({t}^{2}+t)+(-4t-4) & = \\ t(t+1)-4(t+1) & = \\ (t-4)(t+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5({t}^{2}-3t-4) & =5(t-4)(t+1)\end{aligned}
$$
